Do consistent dummy checks for GDRF functions that might take fitted values

Source: R/tseffects.R
GDRF.dummy.checks.Rd

Do consistent dummy checks for GDRF functions that might take fitted values

Usage

GDRF.dummy.checks(
  effect.type,
  prediction.values,
  baseline.y,
  baseline.y.se,
  shock.size,
  d.y,
  inferences.y,
  type = NULL
)

Arguments

effect.type

a character string indicating whether to return discrete effects or fitted values. discrete returns the GDRF as a discrete effect estimate. fitted returns the GDRF as a fitted value, relative to a baseline value of the dependent variable. The default is discrete

prediction.values

a named list of values for non-y variables in the model, used to calculate a steady-state baseline of the dependent variable when effect.type = "fitted" and d.y = 0 and baseline.y is not supplied. Model-based uncertainty will be calculated around the formula for this value. If any differenced variables are included in the model, they should be set to 0. If multiple lags of the same variable are included, they should be set to the same value. Ignored when d.y > 0

baseline.y

a numeric value for the user-supplied baseline value of y in levels (i.e. the baseline value for effects to accumulate from). Only used when effect.type = "fitted". For d.y = 0, this overrides the steady-state calculation from prediction.values if provided

baseline.y.se

a numeric value for the user-supplied standard error for the baseline value of y (to suggest uncertainty around predictions). Only used when effect.type = "fitted" and inferences.y = "levels". If supplied, this is added in quadrature to the standard errors of the GDRF estimates. The default is 0: in recognition that this is user-constructed uncertainty. Possible values would be the square root of the standard deviation of y (in levels)

shock.size

a numeric value for the size of the shock to x in the units of x. Defaults to 1 (a discrete effect similar to traditional marginal effects)

d.y

an integer describing how many times the dependent variable was differenced before model estimation

inferences.y

a character string specifying whether the shock to the independent variable is interpreted in levels or differences (of the dependent variable). Valid arguments include levels or differences. (For y variables where d.y is 0, this is automatically levels.) The default is levels

type

a character string whether the effects are estimated from a GDRF model or the interaction model. Accepts either GDRF or interact

Value

nothing is returned

Author

Soren Jordan, Garrett N. Vande Kamp, and Reshi Rajan
